request.message: I've had a fever for 3 days with a bad headache, and I got bitten by mosquitoes last week

response.message:
Thanks for sharing those details. A fever that has lasted 3 days, along with a bad headache, is worth taking seriously — especially with the mosquito bites and the current dengue advisory in your area. While this could be a common viral illness, it could also be dengue, and we can't tell the difference through chat alone. The best move is to have a doctor check you within the next 24 to 48 hours; a simple blood test can give you a clear answer.

One important thing: with dengue, the most dangerous signs sometimes appear after the fever starts to go down. Even if you feel better in a day or two, keep watching for the signs I've listed below.
response.explanation: A 3-day fever with a bad headache, in the context of recent mosquito exposure and an active dengue advisory, requires a medical evaluation within 24-48 hours.
watch_for: Severe stomach pain
Repeated vomiting
Bleeding gums or nosebleeds
Extreme sleepiness or difficulty waking up
Any of these signs mean you should go to the emergency room immediately
response.next_step: See a doctor within the next 24-48 hours for a check-up and blood test.
self_care: Rest
Drink plenty of water
Paracetamol for the fever if needed, following the package directions
monitoring: Keep track of how you feel for the next 48 hours, even if the fever improves
response.encouragement: I'm here if anything changes or if you have more questions — just let me know.

request.message: May lagnat ako 3 days na tapos sobrang sakit ng ulo ko, nakagat ako ng lamok last week

response.message:
Salamat sa pagdetalye. Ang lagnat na tatlong araw na, kasabay ng matinding sakit ng ulo at pagkagat ng lamok, ay dapat seryosohin. Maaaring trangkaso lang ito, pero dahil sa dami ng kaso ng dengue sa ating lugar ngayon, kailangan nating masigurado na hindi iyon ang dahilan. Hindi natin ito masisiguro sa chat lang, kaya ang pinakaligtas na gawin ay magpa-check sa doktor sa loob ng 1-2 araw para sa isang simpleng blood test.

Kahit na sa tingin mo ay bumubuti ka na, bantayan mo pa rin ang mga senyales sa ibaba sa susunod na 1-2 araw, dahil minsan ay pagkatapos ng lagnat lumalabas ang mga delikadong sintomas ng dengue.
response.explanation: Ang lagnat na tumagal na ng tatlong araw na may kasamang matinding sakit ng ulo, sa gitna ng dengue advisory, ay nangangailangan ng pagsusuri ng doktor sa loob ng 1-2 araw.
watch_for: Matinding sakit ng tiyan o paulit-ulit na pagsusuka
Pagdurugo ng gilagid o ilong
Sobrang tamlay o hirap gisingin
Pantal sa balat
response.next_step: Magpa-check sa doktor sa loob ng 1-2 araw para sa blood test.
self_care: Uminom ng maraming tubig
Magpahinga nang maigi
Paracetamol para sa lagnat kung kailangan, ayon sa nakasulat sa box
monitoring: I-check ang temperatura tuwing 4-6 na oras
Bantayan ang pakiramdam kahit bumaba na ang lagnat
response.encouragement: Nandito lang ako — sabihin mo kung may magbago o may bago kang maramdaman, ha.

history.content: I've had a headache since this morning
Thanks for telling me. One question so I can help better: how bad is the headache right now — mild, moderate, or severe?

response.message:
Salamat sa pagsabi. Dahil lumalala yung sakit ng ulo mo, kailangan nating maging maingat. Kadalasan, ang sakit ng ulo ay puyat, stress, o migraine lang, pero may mga pagkakataon na ang lumalalang sakit ay senyales ng mas seryosong kondisyon na hindi natin masisiguro sa chat lang — walang nakatingin sa'yo at walang pagsusuri na nagawa.

Ang payo ko: magpa-check ka na sa doktor ngayong araw mismo, sa ospital o clinic. Hindi ito para takutin ka, pero mas maigi nang masuri agad habang madali pang maagapan ang anumang dahilan nito. Kung simple lang pala ang sanhi, mas mapapanatag ka rin.
response.explanation: Ang sakit ng ulo na lumalala ay nangangailangan ng pagsusuri ng doktor ngayong araw upang ma-rule out ang mga seryosong sanhi na hindi kayang matukoy sa chat.
watch_for: Biglang paglala ng sakit ng ulo na parang pinakamalalang sakit na naramdaman mo
Panlalabo ng paningin, panghihina ng katawan, o hirap sa pagsasalita
Lagnat na may kasamang matigas na leeg
Pagkalito o pagkawala ng malay
response.next_step: Pumunta sa pinakamalapit na ospital o clinic ngayong araw para magpa-check.
response.encouragement: Tama ang desisyon mong magpa-check ngayon — sabihan mo ako kung kumusta ka pagkatapos.
response.reassessment_reason: Ang paglala ng sakit ng ulo ay nangangailangan ng mas mabilis na atensyong medikal kaysa sa naunang pagtatasa.

request.message: My dog bit me this morning and now I'm feeling feverish and weak

response.message:
I'm sorry to hear about the dog bite. A bite that breaks the skin, followed by feeling feverish and weak, is something that needs a doctor's attention today. Even if the wound looks small, dog bites can introduce bacteria that lead to infections, and there is also the risk of rabies depending on the dog's vaccination status. Because we can't examine the wound or the dog's history here, it's safer to have a professional check this right away.

Please go to the nearest emergency room or a clinic that handles animal bites today. When you arrive, tell the staff: "I was bitten by a dog this morning and I am now feeling feverish and weak."
response.explanation: A dog bite followed by systemic symptoms like fever and weakness requires immediate medical evaluation to assess for infection and rabies risk.
watch_for: Increased redness, swelling, or warmth around the bite
Pus or drainage from the wound
Fever that gets higher or shaking chills
Feeling faint, dizzy, or confused
response.next_step: Go to the nearest emergency room or clinic today — do not wait.
self_care: Wash the bite area gently with soap and running water for several minutes
Cover the wound with a clean, dry bandage
Keep the area elevated if possible
response.encouragement: You are doing the right thing by getting this checked immediately — I'm here if you have any other questions.
